children: By Tomohiko Kanai / Yomiuri Shimbun Staff Writer

Shimadzu Corp. announced on Wednesday that it has restructured three of its U.K. group companies and begun operations under the new structure. The company aims to strengthen its development of mass spectrometers and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy instruments.

Shimadzu Research Laboratory (Europe) Ltd. has been merged into the surviving company Kratos Analytical Ltd., which handles the development and manufacture of mass spectrometers. Personnel from the Mass Spectrometry Business Unit Overseas of Shimadzu UK Ltd. have also been transferred to Kratos.

Mass spectrometers and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy instruments are critical devices used in research and development across fields such as healthcare, drug discovery, food and semiconductors; Shimadzu aims to strengthen its capabilities by consolidating its development and manufacturing bases.
Shimadzu Executive Research Fellow Koichi Tanaka, who won the 2002 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, worked for six years at Shimadzu group companies based in the United Kingdom.
